content: Closed the gap the user caught: every phase now has a deterministic, zero-reasoning script instead of an agent hand-composing JSON and calling write_file. The split matters beyond tidiness -- running these scripts for real (not just authoring them) surfaced three genuine bugs that reading the code would not have: a blank trail_id under -TrailPath, Windows PowerShell 5.1 silently corrupting array-valued fields through ConvertTo-Json unless re-wrapped, and a hand-off bug counting non-Maker plan steps as still owed to Maker. This is the same 'real execution surfaces real bugs' pattern that has recurred all session (the zip path-separator bug, the missing-description warning, the agent-filename rule) -- now applied to the trail-writing mechanism itself, closing a real inconsistency between what Trail-as-Product preaches (schema-conformant, not hand-typed) and what this repo was actually doing to produce every trail before this cycle.

next_seed.summary: pmcro-trail:initialize's link path (an existing --trail-id supplied to orchestrate run) has no deterministic script of its own -- New-Trail.ps1 only implements mint and explicitly rejects an already-existing trail. Orchestrator's New-OrchestrateFrame.ps1 covers claiming/verifying a trail is open and unclaimed, but nothing verifies it was actually materialized by pmcro-trail's own initialize contract. Give pmcro-trail a real link-path script (or an -Link mode on New-Trail.ps1) so that half of its own command contract isn't still aspirational.
